questions.title: How does the Eighth Circuit distinguish intrinsic evidence from Rule 404(b) in prior possession-of-the-same-gun cases?
questions.question_body: The opinion treats D.F. and C.F.'s testimony that they saw Cutbank with the same sawed-off rifle previously as 'intrinsic' rather than 404(b) propensity evidence, citing United States v. Battle. I'm confused about the line the Eighth Circuit draws here: when is prior possession of the same firearm considered intrinsic (and thus admissible without 404(b) analysis) versus extrinsic 404(b) evidence? What facts typically make prior sightings of the same weapon 'directly relevant' to proving later possession rather than impermissible character evidence?

questions.title: Are victim statements admitted to explain police conduct non-hearsay, and when is a limiting instruction required?
questions.question_body: The defendant asked for a preemptive instruction telling the jury not to consider D.F.'s statements to police for their truth until she testified. The court declined, and the panel says no hearsay was admitted and the Confrontation Clause was satisfied because D.F. testified. In the Eighth Circuit, when officers testify about out-of-court statements for 'context' or to explain their actions, is that categorically non-hearsay? How do courts police the line between 'background' and backdoor hearsay, and under what circumstances must a limiting instruction be given at the time of admission versus at the close of trial?

questions.title: Did admitting testimony that the victim’s sister was killed by a gun risk Rule 403 unfair prejudice?
questions.question_body: On cross, defense impeached D.F. with prior inconsistent statements about the gun; in explaining her discomfort with guns, she said her sister was killed by a gun. The court denied a motion to strike, and the panel found no unfair prejudice. Under Rule 403, how do courts weigh probative value (explaining inconsistencies/bias) against the risk the jury will be inflamed by a sympathetic, unrelated death? Are there Eighth Circuit cases addressing similar 'context-of-witness-bias' facts that still warranted exclusion or a limiting instruction?

questions.title: How can a defendant impeach a witness with statements reflected only in a police report the witness did not author?
questions.question_body: Defense tried to read from the investigator's report to impeach C.F., but the court barred it for lack of authentication since C.F. didn't write it. What are the proper routes to get these inconsistencies before the jury: (1) laying a Rule 613(b) foundation and asking the witness about the specific statement without introducing the report; (2) calling the officer/report author to authenticate; (3) using recorded recollection or past recollection refreshed; or (4) prior statements adopted by the witness? In practice, what foundation is required in the Eighth Circuit to use a police report for impeachment when the witness didn't write or sign it?

questions.title: Can the court rely on uncharged conduct in the PSR to apply § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B), and are there any Apprendi/Confrontation concerns?
questions.question_body: The four-level enhancement for possessing a firearm 'in connection with another felony offense' was applied based on PSR facts that were adopted without objection. What evidentiary standard applies at federal sentencing for such uncharged conduct (preponderance?), and is the court permitted to rely solely on the PSR absent live testimony if the defendant doesn't object? Also, does Apprendi/Booker require jury findings for this enhancement when it increases the advisory range but not the statutory maximum, and are there any Sixth Amendment or Confrontation Clause limits on using hearsay within the PSR?

questions.title: How do ACCA’s § 4B1.4 offense levels interact with § 2K2.1 and specific offense characteristics without double counting?
questions.question_body: The court notes the Armed Career Criminal Guideline would produce an offense level of 34, but the court used a higher total offense level (35) after applying § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) and other enhancements, because the Guidelines say use the greater offense level. Is it standard to calculate both paths (ACCA § 4B1.4 vs. § 2K2.1 with SOCs) and choose the higher? When do enhancements like altered/obliterated serial number or reckless endangerment during flight risk impermissible double counting with § 4B1.4? Any Eighth Circuit authority clarifying the boundaries?

questions.title: What level of explanation must a district judge give when imposing a within-Guidelines sentence to show consideration of § 3553(a)?
questions.question_body: The panel presumes reasonableness for a within-range sentence and says no 'mechanical recitation' is required so long as the record shows the court considered § 3553(a). How much engagement with defense mitigation is required in the Eighth Circuit? If the court references reviewing the PSR and memoranda and mentions some § 3553(a) factors, is that sufficient even when the defense argues the range is inflated by enhancements? Are there cases where a within-Guidelines sentence was reversed for inadequate explanation?

questions.title: Can an appellee broaden the issues on appeal, and how does that affect standards of review and party presentation?
questions.question_body: The panel criticizes the government for 'unnecessarily expand[ing] the issues on appeal' by framing a claim about thwarted cross-examination that appellant didn’t clearly brief. What is the Eighth Circuit’s approach to the party presentation principle in criminal appeals? If the government raises an additional framing or justification, will the court consider it, disregard it, or resolve it under plain error? How does this interact with forfeiture vs. waiver of objections made (or not) in the district court and in the opening brief?
